newsitem.title: BURMA: Burmese students move protest to streets.
newsitem.headline: Burmese students move protest to streets.

text.p: Hundreds of Burmese students, some of whom had been staging a peaceful sit-in protest on a Rangoon campus, took their demonstration to the streets on Monday, witnesses said.

A group of about 700 students left the Yangon Institute of Technology (YIT) campus and was heading in the direction of another campus in Rangoon, witnesses said. Earlier, about 100 YIT students staged a sit-in protest to show their displeasure at leaflets urging them to improve their behaviour.
The sit-in protest was also related to police handling of a brawl between students and restaurant owners that led to a rare street demonstration by about 500 university students in October.
"The students who were staging the sit-in protest have grown in number and now have left the YIT campus and are marching towards another campus," one eyewitness told Reuters.
A YIT source said the demonstrating students left the campus and took to the streets after education ministry officials refused to accept their demands.

The students had made a series of demands related to the leaflets and the October brawl, YIT sources said. Three students were temporarily arrested and two ordered not to attend classes in connection with the brawl.
